<description>
The HTTP server runs requests that are already in its receive buffer after it has queued a reply that closes the connection. RFC 9112 section 9.6 says it must not. This is a regression from #35182, which replaced libevent: libevent's `evhttp_send_done()` frees the connection once a closing reply is sent, so buffered requests were never parsed. The server also keeps the connection open after a request with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding. Section 6.1 says it must close it. Until both are fixed, a request sent right behind a request with both headers is run.

The first commit stops reading requests from a client once a closing reply is queued or the client is flagged for disconnection. Its code and unit tests are azuchi's work from #36355, which was closed. The second commit makes `WriteReply()` send "Connection: close" for a request with both headers, so the server closes the connection. It extends the Content-Length plus Transfer-Encoding case in `interface_http.py`: a `setnetworkactive false` request sent right behind it must not run, and the only reply must say "Connection: close". Tested with `test_bitcoin --run_test=httpserver_tests` and the functional tests `interface_http.py`, `interface_rpc.py` and `interface_rest.py`, which pass.
</description>

<commits>
8b1a97923d http: stop reading after a closing reply

After a reply that closes the connection is queued, the server still
parses requests already in its receive buffer. It runs them. If the
closing reply is still being sent, a keep-alive request behind it also
keeps the connection open. RFC 9112 section 9.6 says a server that sends
a close must not process further requests on that connection.

`Send()` now sets `m_closing` when the reply is not keep-alive.
`TryReadRequest()` returns nothing for a client with `m_closing` or
`m_disconnect` set. From #36355. Two new unit tests cover a closing
reply that is flushed at once and one that stays queued. The existing
two-request unit test now asks for keep-alive.

cdd831035d http: close connection on conflicting framing

The HTTP server keeps the connection open after it answers a request
with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding. RFC 9112 section 6.1
says the server must close the connection after responding to such a
request.

`HTTPRequest::WriteReply()` now sends "Connection: close" in that case,
as it does when the client asks for it. The server then closes the
connection. The request itself is processed as before. The
Content-Length plus Transfer-Encoding case in `interface_http.py` now
sends a `setnetworkactive false` request right behind it. The test
checks that a single reply comes back, with "Connection: close", and
that the network stays active.
</commits>
